QUOTE_VERBATIM:
Classify the final execution context before assessing impact:<sup>[[8]](#references)[[9]](#references)</sup>
 Context | What successful injection normally gains | What to verify |
 Host-page DOM modified by a content script | JavaScript in the web page's main world, not automatic access to the content script's isolated-world privileges | Page CSP and whether a DOM or window.postMessage bridge forwards attacker data to the content script |
 Ordinary extension page (popup, options page, or reachable extension HTML) | The extension origin and the extension APIs available to that page | The extension-page CSP, manifest permissions, and any runtime-message handlers reachable from the page |
 Manifest V2 background page | A privileged extension page with a DOM | Whether attacker data reaches an HTML/code-execution sink through messaging or stored state |
 Manifest V3 service worker | No DOM, so this is a message/API or code-injection review rather than DOM XSS | Untrusted messages, unsafe URL/API arguments, and dynamic-code sinks |
 Page listed in sandbox.pages | Script allowed by the sandbox's separate CSP, but in a unique origin without extension APIs or direct access to non-sandboxed pages | Whether a privileged parent trusts messages from the sandbox and exposes an unsafe postMessage bridge |

The sandbox case is an important exception to the usual MV3 CSP rule.
